reasoning: The original skill set is too large and deep to master within 6 months if the goal is job-ready (breadth + depth across many languages, cloud providers, orchestration platforms, and advanced topics). To be realistic I kept a focused, high-impact subset that balances fundamentals, backend development, databases, cloud/deployment basics, and software architecture/operational skills. I prioritized one primary language and framework (Python + FastAPI), core CS fundamentals, source control and CI/CD, a single relational DB (Postgres/SQL) plus basic NoSQL concepts, containerization, and essential professional skills. Many overlapping or lower-impact items (multiple backend languages, multiple cloud providers, full Kubernetes mastery, enterprise frameworks for other languages, and many niche tools) were removed or deferred to post-hire learning. This reduced list is aimed at achievable, demonstrable job-readiness in 6 months.

fundamentals.name: Data Structures
fundamentals.reason: Essential for algorithmic problem solving and interview readiness.

fundamentals.name: Algorithms
fundamentals.reason: Needed for performance-aware code and coding interviews.

fundamentals.name: Object-Oriented Programming
fundamentals.reason: Core paradigm for structuring maintainable backend code.

fundamentals.name: Software Development (practices)
fundamentals.reason: Covers design, modularity, code reviews and maintainability.

fundamentals.name: Computer Science fundamentals
fundamentals.reason: Core concepts (complexity, memory, concurrency basics) that underlie backend systems.

fundamentals.name: Linux basics
fundamentals.reason: Working knowledge of Linux is required for development, debugging and deployment.

frameworks_and_runtime.name: Python
frameworks_and_runtime.reason: High-impact, versatile backend language; lets you build APIs, scripts and prototypes quickly.

frameworks_and_runtime.name: FastAPI
frameworks_and_runtime.reason: Modern, fast Python web framework used for building APIs with good performance and developer ergonomics.

frameworks_and_runtime.name: Node.js (basic familiarity)
frameworks_and_runtime.reason: Useful to understand JS backend concepts and run small full-stack tasks; kept as secondary familiarity, not a primary deep focus.

frameworks_and_runtime.name: TypeScript (basic)
frameworks_and_runtime.reason: Strongly-typed JS improves reliability for API clients and small full-stack work; a practical companion to Node.js.

databases.name: SQL (relational fundamentals)
databases.reason: Critical for data modelling, querying and transactions in most backend roles.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.reason: Industry-favored open-source relational DB with advanced features suitable for most backend apps.

databases.name: NoSQL (concepts and MongoDB basics)

version_control_and_ci_cd.name: Docker

version_control_and_ci_cd.name: CI/CD (practical pipelines)
version_control_and_ci_cd.reason: Automates testing and deployments — necessary to ship reliably; focus on GitHub Actions or GitLab CI for hands-on pipelines.

testing_and_debugging.name: Unit testing (pytest)
testing_and_debugging.reason: Verifies functionality of components; pytest is the practical Python toolkit to learn.

testing_and_debugging.name: Software testing (integration/basic E2E)
testing_and_debugging.reason: Integration tests and basic end-to-end checks prevent regressions in multi-component apps.

testing_and_debugging.name: Debugging & Troubleshooting
testing_and_debugging.reason: Hands-on skill for diagnosing production and development issues efficiently.

testing_and_debugging.name: TDD (conceptual)
testing_and_debugging.reason: Test-driven development principles improve design and test coverage; keep as a practice to adopt gradually.

api_and_networking.name: REST APIs

api_and_networking.name: GraphQL (conceptual)
